correctness.rationale: The exact killed-generator first-step equations yield \(H_{ij}=1/r_i+ k/r_j\) for distinct leaves. Therefore the worst ordered-pair expectation equals k times the largest reciprocal rate plus the second largest. Budget saturation and replacement of any smaller reciprocal waiting time by the second largest prove that every optimizer has at most one larger wait. Exchange assigns that wait to a highest-price edge. The resulting scalar ratio objective \((kp+P+kPt+p/t)/B\) is strictly convex on \(t\ge1\), proving a unique minimizer and the exact premium-price threshold. Exact rational hitting-system elimination and deterministic feasible-competitor tests replayed successfully; finite tests are supplemental.

value.rationale: For every star size \(k\ge3\) and all positive individual edge prices, this is a complete non-obvious resource-allocation classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice: a strong equal-rate regime persists under heterogeneous prices and then gives way to one uniquely slower premium edge at the exact natural boundary \(p=kP\). The closed improvement \((\sqrt p-\sqrt{kP})_+^2/B\) quantifies the practical and mathematical threshold. These features are not determined by known unweighted star topology extremality, generic hitting identities or spectral-gap allocation.
